subject: Advice on properly setting up shiny server so that apps are resolved and don't return 404?

messages.author: a1bf76ab9a5a2d4b
messages.subject: Advice on properly setting up shiny server so that apps are resolved and don't return 404?
parts:
I have a shiny server installed on a virtual server.  The shiny apps work, but using `curl` on the app URL results in a 404. This is becoming a problem for me because my CRAN packages include links to my shiny apps, and `R CMD check` results in a NOTE about invalid URL because of the 404.

To reproduce, I just spun up a brand new server (using DigitalOcean), installed R, shiny, and shiny server, and haven't done any further configuration.

Here is the URL of the sample app that is available when installing shiny server
http://104.236.169.84:3838/sample-apps/hello/

But running `curl -I -L http://104.236.169.84:3838/sample-apps/hello/` returns
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
x-ua-compatible: IE=edge,chrome=1
content-type: text/html; charset=UTF-8
content-length: 18
connection: keep-alive
Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2015 21:21:22 GMT


If I run a similar command on http://104.236.169.84:3838/sample-apps/ or http://104.236.169.84:3838/ then I get `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`

Is there an easy way to fix the configuration so that shiny apps will return successful headers?

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Advice on properly setting up shiny server so that apps are resolved and don't return 404?
parts: I don't think this is shiny server; it's just Shiny/httpuv not supporting HEAD and returning 404. If you remove the -I from the curl command it works.
